I have a proposal for you, Director.
Won't you please kill me?
I would like to put this little prop to good use.
However, adult videos have a mosaic blur.
So unfortunately, we cannot show the most crucial part of how deeply you are feeling.
That is why we will use this whistle. Please try blowing it.
Ah, what a nice sound. One more time.
When you begin to feel fairly good, please blow that whistle once.
When you feel even more, blow twice—and when you simply cannot bear it anymore, three times.
By using this whistle, viewers will be able to tell the exact degree of your pleasure.

meanings.note: Polite form is おはようございます.

examples.trans: Good morning, did you sleep well?

examples.text: みんなにおはようと言う。

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: 全員が幸せになれる提案だよ、これは。
examples.trans: This is a proposal that makes everyone happy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Godan verb.

examples.text: このペンを使ってもいいですか。
もっと英語を使いましょう。

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; takes を or と.

examples.text: 季節の変化を感じます。
examples.trans: I feel the change of seasons.

examples.text: 少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
examples.trans: You may feel it's a little expensive.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Noun.

examples.text: 心を開いて話しましょう。
examples.trans: Let's open our hearts and talk.

examples.text: 温かい心に感謝します。
examples.trans: I'm grateful for your warm heart.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Conjunction introducing a solution or next step based on the preceding situation.

examples.text: そこで新しい方法を試しました。
examples.trans: So, we tried a new method.

examples.text: そこでこの道具が役に立ちます。
examples.trans: That is where this tool comes in handy.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Humble counterpart of もらう; volitional いただこう means 'let's take them / I'll have them'.

forms.title: Key forms of いただく

examples.text: お時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you spare me some time?

meanings.note: Intensifies the following adverb or verb, as in もっとちゃんと見て.

examples.text: もっと近くで見てください。
もっとゆっくり話してください。
もっと感じてきたなという時には二回。もうこれはたまらないなという時には三回。
examples.trans: When you feel even more, blow twice—and when you simply cannot bear it anymore, three times.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: もっと感じてきたなという時には二回。もうこれはたまらないなという時には三回。
examples.trans: When you feel even more, blow twice—and when you simply cannot bear it anymore, three times.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
